answer: Require each agent to lock a nontransferable stake before its claims can earn rewards, then slash that stake when independent audits prove duplicated identities. The tundra of cheap accounts is screened by a real opportunity cost: an opal-sized claim still requires a full bond, and a vault holding that bond remains at risk until the audit window closes. A Sybil operator therefore funds and risks one bond per identity, while honest agents recover theirs.
